overlaps.summary: The overlap most likely concentrates in adults 40-54, though younger lifters (25-39) come close.
overlaps.logic: Share of the overlap aged 40-54. 40-54 is the largest cell for medication users (int_1: 0.40, ev_21) but not for weekly lifters (int_2: 0.35; their largest is 25-39 at 0.45). Low 0.35 = the smaller of the two groups' own 40-54 shares (no concentration effect). High 0.43 = product rule: 0.40x0.35 / (0.25x0.45 + 0.40x0.35 + 0.35x0.20) = 0.14/0.3225, assuming medication use and lifting are independent within each age band and bands are equal size. Weighting bands by width (15/15/10 years) gives 0.39, inside the range. Under the product rule 40-54 is the overlap's largest cell (0.43 vs 0.35 for 25-39). No source publishes the joint number; int_2's shares are uncited demo values.

size.logic: US adults 25-64: 170M (ev_20) x GLP-1 use 1/8 (ev_15) = 21.25M users. x share aged 40-60: 0.40 (40-54) + 0.35 x 6/10 (40-60's part of 55-64, assuming an even spread) = 0.61 (ev_21) -> 12.96M. x 14% who strength-train weekly at 40-60 (ev_22, assumed the same for medication users) = 1,814,750, rounded to 1.81M.

serviceability.motivation: Noticing strength loss now, and afraid of regaining weight when they stop the medication.
serviceability.reasoning: The leading tracker is well rated but its reviews show muscle retention going unaddressed; switching language is present, and the group is well above the minimum size.

values.value: aware of the problem, not searching

size.logic: US adults 25-64: 170M (ev_20) x GLP-1 use 1/8 (ev_15) = 21.25M users. x share aged 35-64, the ad range: 0.25 x 5/15 (35-39's part of 25-39, even spread assumed) + 0.40 + 0.35 = 0.833 (ev_21) -> 17.71M. x 1/3 who started within the past year (ev_24) -> 5.90M. x 40% who never followed a workout plan (ev_22, a 40-60 figure applied to 35-64) = 2,361,111, rounded to 2.36M.

serviceability.motivation: Just started medication and wants a plan, but has quit generic apps before.
serviceability.reasoning: Large group, but evidence is thin (few excerpts), the owner's broad 'GLP-1' ad was inconclusive, and free beginner options are already well rated (FreeFit, 850K ratings, ev_23).

findings.claim: Losing muscle is the most common concern among midlife strength protectors.
findings.derivation: Script count of concern tags across this group's excerpts (see concernBundles).
findings.limitations: Demo data; forum posters skew toward people having problems

findings.claim: The muscle-focused Meta ad cost less per sign-up than the most you can spend to win a customer; the broad 'GLP-1 journey' ad was inconclusive.
findings.derivation: Script-computed verdicts from meta-ads.csv, judged against the most you can spend to win a customer, worked out from your numbers (price, purchases per year, acquisition share).

findings.claim: The leading calorie tracker is well rated but doesn't address keeping muscle during weight loss.
findings.derivation: High aggregate rating plus reviews and posts asking for muscle help that the app lacks.

findings.claim: Midlife strength protectors number about 1.8M US adults, well above the minimum this business needs.
findings.derivation: 170M US adults 25-64 (ev_20) x 1/8 GLP-1 use (ev_15) x 0.61 aged 40-60 (ev_21) x 14% weekly strength training (ev_22) = 1.81M; compared with the script's minPopulation.
findings.limitations: Fictional demo inputs; ev_15 counts anyone who has ever used the medication, and the exercise rate is for all adults 40-60, not medication users

findings.claim: The owner's original broad group ('people on GLP-1s, new to fitness') is crowded with free options and its evidence is thin.
findings.derivation: A free beginner app rated 4.6 from 850K ratings (ev_23), few excerpts for this group, an inconclusive broad ad, and switching-away language about generic apps.
